newsitem.title: USA: Lukens Medical sees hefty 1997 revs growth.
newsitem.headline: Lukens Medical sees hefty 1997 revs growth.

text.p: Lukens Medical Corp. President and Chief Executive Officer Robert Huffstodt said he expects substantial revenue growth in 1997 with the expansion of Third World and U.S. sales.
Huffstodt said U.S. sales of the disposable medical products company were growing steadily and that he expected "some very substantial growth in our suture business in the Third World."

Huffstodt told Reuters in a telephone interview he was "comfortable" with analysts' estimates that Lukens would post 1997 revenues of between $14 million and $16 million and earnings per share of between $0.45 and $0.50.
For the first nine months of 1996, Lukens had net income of $574,000, or $0.19 per share, on revenues of $6.14 million.

Huffstodt said Lukens' recently acquired hypodermic needle and syringe facility in southern India would produce revenues of $1.5 million in 1997 and reach its full, $300,000 monthly-sales capacity by the end of 1997.

He said strong revenues would come from U.S. sales of veterinarian and dental product lines, and that Lukens is looking to expand its suture production facilities outside of the United States during the second or third quarter of 1997, possibly to India.
